Connected case study · SURF-IT

Land-cover classification and segment analysis.

This companion study turns a four-class land-cover map into segment-level context variables for embankment analysis. A Google Earth Engine classification was used to measure how much river, aquaculture, crop and settlement area occurs around each embankment segment, including separate river-side and land-side percentages.

4mapped land-cover categories

Project scope

A compact landscape layer for each embankment segment.

The goal was not to create another hazard model, but to summarise the landscape around the embankments in a consistent way. The resulting land-cover percentages can later be joined with the LiDAR-derived elevation and geometry indicators from the first case study.

ImageryPlanet 2026 composite, with Sentinel-2 views used during interpretation
ClassificationGoogle Earth Engine · Random Forest
ClassesRiver · Aquaculture · Crop · Settlement
ExtractionJupyter Notebook · segment-wise area and percentage summaries

Workflow

Three steps, one connected output.

Step 01

Prepare imagery

Planet imagery and spectral indices were assembled in Google Earth Engine to support visual interpretation and training data preparation.

Step 02

Classify land cover

A Random Forest classifier produced a four-class LULC map for the full SURF-IT study area.

Step 03

Extract percentages

The classified map was summarised by segment so each embankment section received side-wise class percentages.

The classification map shown above is the main spatial input for the segment statistics. The code itself is not reproduced here, since this page focuses on the workflow and outputs rather than the full script.

Segment extraction

Side-wise percentages were measured against the real embankment setting.

The orthomosaic below illustrates the logic used in the extraction stage. Each segment buffer was interpreted in relation to the embankment alignment, then split into river-facing and land-facing sides before the class percentages were calculated.

Orthomosaic with embankment alignment overlay used to explain river-side and land-side contextSegment-based interpretation
Segment ID retainedEach percentage record stays linked to the original embankment segment geometry.
Side-wise percentagesLand-cover shares were calculated separately for the river side and the land side.
Analysis-ready tablesThe final outputs are tidy tables that can be joined back to GIS layers or used in later modelling.
